subject: [RFC PATCH v2 01/18] mm: free PG_rcu_free folios only after an RCU grace period

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new page flag, PG_rcu_free, which allows folios to be freed only after an RCU (Read-Copy Update) grace period. This is done to prevent CPUs from bouncing the refcount of a file being read, and to allow readers to access the folio until the RCU grace period has passed. The patch adds support for this flag in various kernel components, including page flags, vmstat, and memory failure handling. It also introduces a new workqueue to handle freeing deferred pages during an RCU grace period.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David suggested renaming PG_rcu_free to FOLIO_RCU_FREE, aligning it with the existing naming convention for folio-specific flags.

Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the patch description does not accurately describe what the basic infrastructure in page_alloc does, and suggested adding a dedicated FOLIO_RCU_FREE config to enable pagecache use.

Reviewer David suggested replacing the PG_rcu_free flag definition with a const mask constructed using BIT() and __PG_RCU_FREE to avoid a growing list of flags, which would be more consistent with other page flags.

Reviewer David suggested moving the handling of PG_rcu_free to mm/folio.c, specifically intercepting on the folio freeing path in __folio_put() before free_frozen_pages(), which is used by other machinery such as slab.
reviews.raw_body:
I think we really want to focus this only on folios (like the current code does).

FOLIO_RCU_FREE ?

---

While that description is helpful, that's not really what this patch, or rather
the basic infrastructure in page_alloc, does.

I'd suggest to have a dedicated FOLIO_RCU_FREE config and maybe another one
(that selects/depends on) FOLIO_RCU_FREE that actually enables the pagecache use
and documents the details.

---

That looks a bit odd at first, as it's very different to the other once. But no
easy way around assuming that the flag is not always around.

Maybe we should just have this be a const mask constructed somewhere using BIT()
and __PG_RCU_FREE etc, instead of having this growing list in this user here.

---

I'm wondering whether we want to intercept on the folio freeing path instead?
That would be __folio_put(), before we go into free_frozen_pages() used by other
machinery that does not apply (slab etc).

So maybe this handling could be placed into mm/folio.c instead, just a quick
thought ... reading about folio batches above I think that might be the right
direction, we are mixing too much page vs. folio things here.

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-11-05.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new page flag, PG_rcu_free, which allows folios to be freed only after an RCU (Read-Copy Update) grace period. This is done to prevent CPUs from bouncing the reference count of a page cache folio while it's being read by multiple processes. The flag is 64-bit only and is disabled on PREEMPT_RT kernels where expedited grace periods are normal. A new workqueue, WQ_MEM_RECLAIM, is used to free batches of pages after an RCU grace period has passed. This patch also introduces a new counter in /proc/vmstat to track the number of deferred pages.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
Author agreed to add a second Kconfig symbol for CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE, but only if it has a second user.

Author agrees that introducing split_copy_flags is necessary before adding the PG_rcu_free flag, plans to restructure in a future patch.

The author addressed David's concern that not all page cache folios are freed through __folio_put(), and explained that reclaim frees them directly with free_unref_folios(). The author added a patch to set the PG_rcu_free flag in __free_pages_prepare() where all folios pass, ensuring it is set for all paths.
reviews.raw_body:
I will make the help describe what this patch does.  The page cache is
the only user, and both symbols would be def_bool without a prompt, so
I would rather add the second one with a second user.

Does that work for you?

---

Makes sense.  Something like the diff below, on top of this patch.
Introducing split_copy_flags would be a preparatory patch, and this one
would only add __PG_RCU_FREE to it.

---

Not all page cache folios are freed through __folio_put().  Reclaim
frees them with free_unref_folios() directly (shrink_folio_list(),
move_folios_to_lru()), and so do folios_put_refs() and the LRU batches.
__free_pages_prepare() is the one place they all pass.

diff --git a/include/linux/page-flags.h b/include/linux/page-flags.h
index a1e52a1f8a52..6d4e534c9ccc 100644
--- a/include/linux/page-flags.h
+++ b/include/linux/page-flags.h
@@ -1185,6 +1185,18 @@ static __always_inline void __ClearPageAnonExclusive(struct page *page)
 #define __PG_MLOCKED		0
 #endif
 
+#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_USES_PG_ARCH_2
+#define __PG_ARCH_2		BIT(PG_arch_2)
+#else
+#define __PG_ARCH_2		0
+#endif
+
+#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_USES_PG_ARCH_3
+#define __PG_ARCH_3		BIT(PG_arch_3)
+#else
+#define __PG_ARCH_3		0
+#endif
+
 /*
  * Flags checked when a page is freed.  Pages being freed should not have
  * these flags set.  If they are, there is a problem.
diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index 25082949a4ca..44a1aaa3f834 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -3689,6 +3689,23 @@ static void __split_folio_to_order(struct folio *folio, int old_order,
 	const bool handle_hwpoison = folio_test_has_hwpoisoned(folio) && new_order;
 	long new_nr_pages = 1 << new_order;
 	long nr_pages = 1 << old_order;
+	const unsigned long split_copy_flags =
+		BIT(PG_referenced) |
+		BIT(PG_swapbacked) |
+		BIT(PG_swapcache) |
+		__PG_MLOCKED |
+		BIT(PG_uptodate) |
+		BIT(PG_active) |
+		BIT(PG_workingset) |
+		BIT(PG_locked) |
+		BIT(PG_unevictable) |
+		__PG_ARCH_2 |
+		__PG_ARCH_3 |
+		BIT(PG_dirty) |
+		BIT(PG_dropbehind) |
+		__PG_RCU_FREE |
+		LRU_GEN_MASK |
+		LRU_REFS_MASK;
 	long i;
 
 	folio_clear_has_hwpoisoned(folio);
@@ -3725,26 +3742,7 @@ static void __split_folio_to_order(struct folio *folio, int old_order,
 		 * PG_anon_exclusive (-> PG_mappedtodisk) for these here.
 		 */
 		new_folio->flags.f &= ~PAGE_FLAGS_CHECK_AT_PREP;
-		new_folio->flags.f |= (folio->flags.f &
-				((1L << PG_referenced) |
-				 (1L << PG_swapbacked) |
-				 (1L << PG_swapcache) |
-				 (1L << PG_mlocked) |
-				 (1L << PG_uptodate) |
-				 (1L << PG_active) |
-				 (1L << PG_workingset) |
-				 (1L << PG_locked) |
-				 (1L << PG_unevictable) |
-#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_USES_PG_ARCH_2
-				 (1L << PG_arch_2) |
-#endif
-#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_USES_PG_ARCH_3
-				 (1L << PG_arch_3) |
-#endif
-				 (1L << PG_dirty) |
-				 (1L << PG_dropbehind) |
-				 __PG_RCU_FREE |
-				 LRU_GEN_MASK | LRU_REFS_MASK));
+		new_folio->flags.f |= folio->flags.f & split_copy_flags;
 
 		new_folio->mapping = folio->mapping;
 		new_folio->index = folio->index + i;
-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) suggested reworking the code to have a clear folio freeing path, specifically proposing to use existing helpers like __folio_put() and free_unref_folios(), and requested that this be done before implementing PG_rcu_free.

Reviewer David suggested using a bitfield for FOLIO_SPLIT_FLAGS to make the function shorter, and proposed an alternative approach of defining it as a static const unsigned long.
reviews.raw_body:
Can we just rework that code first to have some clear folio freeing path, IOW
doing this in a folio-specific helper?

folios_put_refs() is just a specialized and batched variant of the __folio_put()
freeing path in the end. So we can hook into these two easily.

For free_unref_folios() would need another hook or a cleaner rework.

---

I was rather thinking of a


#define FOLIO_SPLIT_FLAGS	BIT(PG_referenced) | BIT(PG_swapbacked) | \

...

To make this function actually shorter :)

(ofc, you could also have a static const unsigned long, if that's what we want)

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that making PG_rcu_free specific to one special freeing path would make the code fragile, less obvious, and limit its potential usefulness and applicability across the kernel.
reviews.raw_body:
I think you're making things worse rather than better.

The whole point was to hook into *one* place: the page freeing.

Trying to make it specific to one special freeing path only makes it
fragile and less obvious, and results in anybody who then uses some
other freeing model to miss the RCU thing.

It also means that suddenly nobody else can use the RCU path for their own uses.

Look at all the kmalloc RCU freeing: it's used all over the place. RCU
has basically taken over the kernel. Every single performance-critical
lock-free area of the kernel wants RCU freeing.

I think trying to corral it into some special case is the last thing
we want to do. It only makes things less potentially useful and more
fragile.

                  Linus

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer noted that the current code only handles folios and will start to fail on pages, which makes the introduction of PG_rcu_free unnecessary as it's intended for page-level functionality.

Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the current patch does not handle folio-specific freeing paths and suggested adding a hook to the folio freeing path, also mentioning the need for a clean path for freeing folios as struct page is being decoupled from struct folio.

Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concern about how the PG_rcu_free flag would work when pages are decoupled from folios, potentially leading to issues with lockless lookups and refcounts.
sentiment_signals: potential issues with lockless lookups and refcounts
reviews.raw_body:
The current code deals with pages vs. folios in ways that already makes this
code only work with folios even in the short term.

We'll be starting to let page_folio() fail soon on things that are not actual
folios. PG_folio for that is already in the works.

---

Right, and I'd hook into the folio freeing path if it is folio-specific.

And we will need clean path for freeing folios either way as we are starting to
decouple struct page from struct folio as envisioned by Willy.

If we actually manage to make this generic for different memdescs in the future,
it can obviously stay on the generic path.

---

Let me wrap my head around how this would look when we decouple pages from
folios, where pages might not have a ->lru anymore, or not even a refcount.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Linus Torvalds pointed out that RCU freeing of pages is already implemented in other areas, such as TLB shootdown, and suggested that the new PG_rcu_free flag could have been designed to be more straightforward if it had been introduced earlier. He noted that existing hacks in this area are complicated due to the complexity of architecture-specific code and would be painful to convert to a new order.
reviews.raw_body:
So for an example of a place that already does RCU freeing of pages -
*not* folios - look at the TLB shootdown.

It's very round-about and hard to tell, but it's using

  tlb_remove_table_free
    call_rcu(&batch->rcu, tlb_remove_table_rcu);

and that then does

  tlb_remove_table_rcu ->
    __tlb_remove_table_free ->
      __tlb_remove_table ->
        pagetable_dtor_free ->
          pagetable_free ->
            __pagetable_free ->
               __free_pages(page, compound_order(page))

(and I might have messed this up - this really is a rats nest of
nested inline functions).

And in order to do this all, it sets up *another* page just to contain
the batching (which is also RCU-free'd)

Now, the batching is probably a very good thing in that context, so
I'm not actually suggesting this should be converted to some common
RCU-freeing thing.

Rather, I'm pointing out that we have existing hacks in this area that
have grown up over time and would have been a *lot* less hacky if we
had had a proper RCU-freeing page allocator back when that whole TLB
freeing code was written.

So I'm not saying "we should unify this". But I *am* saying "look, RCU
freeing of pages is _already_ a thing, and we have complicated hacky
things in place for it".

And they are complicated not because they necessarily should be
complicated, but because we solved the TLB shootdown after we already
had tons of complex architecture-specific code in place, and we
basically ended up adding that RCU phase on top of that existing
per-architecture complexity and abstraction.

*NOW* it would be actually fairly painful to try to convert the TLB
shootdown to a new order. But originally, it would have been very nice
if we had just had a "Oh, mark this page for RCU freeing".

(In all fairness, we also did it that way because some architectures
don't need the RCU delay simply because they have some other hardware
page walking infrastructure than the actual page tables the kernel
builds up. Not that those architectures *matter* today, but some of
that per-architecture inline function stuff is required to basically
isolate these kinds of decisions from the MM code - that deep inline
function indirection has a reason that is entirely independent of the
freeing side).

                    Linus

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the current implementation may not work on certain architectures due to issues with ->lru and multiple page tables residing in a single physical page, which could lead to freeing only parts of a page instead of full pages. He mentioned that some page tables are already allocated from slab on sparc64 and m68k, and that tlb_remove_table() consumes a void * pointer instead of a page/ptdesc pointer due to these complexities.

Reviewer David expressed concern about the patch's interaction with CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TLB_REMOVE_TABLE, specifically mentioning powerpc as an affected architecture, and suggested that the patch may not be suitable for all platforms.

Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concerns that RCU freeing of memdescs will require keeping them alive until their physical pages are freed, and suggested this may be specific to each type of memdesc.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, I recall some details about ->lru not being usable (as reused for other
purposes by some architectures) and some things about multiple page tables
residing in a single physical page on some architectures (at least powerpc),
which makes using ptdesc / ->lru impossible as well, as we might only be freeing
parts of a page instead of full pages.

And some page tables today might already be allocated from slab (I think at
least sparc64 and m68k do that).

So that's one of the reason why tlb_remove_table() consumes a void * pointer
instead of a page/ptdesc pointer. It's all linked to
CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TLB_REMOVE_TABLE IIRC.

---

See, I am not sure about that given the challenge with
CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TLB_REMOVE_TABLE. And apparently powerpc is using that, which
is not quite the museum piece (compared to m68k and sparc64 :) )

In a perfect world without these corner cases that make our life hard, possibly.

---

There are some dirty details when it comes to the upcoming page vs. folio split
that I am still unclear about.

The page table example you mention above is another prime example of the
challenges we'll face: page tables will have a separately allocated memdesc
("ptdesc"), just like folios will have their memdesc ("folio") separately allocated.

When RCU freeing, we'll really have to keep the allocated memdesc alive as well.
RCU-freeing the page only is not sufficient.

There was even talk about allocating page tables from slab later, as long as we
can adjust a "struct ptdesc" to it. Which would solve the problem of powerpc
etc. that don't operate on full pages for page tables.

So I might be completely off, but what I imagine is that the memdescs will get
RCU-freed (these are not pages), and once they are then getting freed, they will
probably take the physical page with them.

And freeing memdescs through RCU will likely be memdesc specific.

I really don't know, Willy might know more about these plans.

But I am overloaded with all the Fixes, so my brain doesn't work quite right.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the lockless read dereferences the folio too, so it needs to wait for the grace period along with its pages. The check will be kept in __free_pages_prepare(), a function where every page cache folio passes.
reviews.raw_body:
Right: once the folio is allocated separately, the lockless read
dereferences it too, so it has to wait for the grace period along with
its pages.  The per-CPU batching and the waits in the allocator later
in the series do not depend on where the check sits.

Until then the folio is the struct page, and __free_pages_prepare() is
the one place every page cache folio passes, so v3 keeps the check
there.  That function already takes page_folio() for the mlock and anon
checks, so making page_folio() fail for non-folios has to handle it
anyway.

Willy, is there a plan for how a folio memdesc gets freed after a grace
period?

The rest of v3 for this patch: CONFIG_FOLIO_RCU_FREE with help text for
what it adds, and FOLIO_SPLIT_FLAGS as a #define in a preparatory patch,
on top of Zi's PG_waiters fix.

I will not post v3 for a while: mm has enough traffic right now.
Unless you say I should.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concern that the implementation is too focused on individual folios, which could lead to inefficiencies and potential issues when dealing with large numbers of folios.
reviews.raw_body:
If we go that way, don't make it effectively folio-centric in the
implementation. That's what triggered my response in the first place.

-- 
Cheers,

David
